;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Afghan peace process]], [[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**An Afghan government spokesman says it will continue to release [[Taliban]] prisoners though disagreement prevails over the release of some 600 of them that are considered a "threat to national security". The Taliban could not be reached for comment and it is not clear whether they are willing to accept to start talks based on the list of prisoners set to be freed. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-afghanistan-taliban-prisoners/afghanistan-to-release-prisoners-from-taliban-list-in-push-for-talks-idUSKBN24A17D (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Sahel]]
**The [[United States]] says it is "deeply concerned" about abuses by state security forces in the [[Sahel]] and threatens to cut aid to the [[G5 Sahel|G5]] nations that form a coalition in the area – [[Burkina Faso]], [[Mali]], [[Mauritania]], [[Niger]], and [[Chad]] – if those issues are not addressed. The U.S. also welcomes a summit to be held between the G5 nations and [[France]] and [[Spain]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sahel-security-usa/u-s-warns-aid-at-risk-unless-alleged-abuses-in-west-africas-sahel-region-addressed-idUSKBN24A223?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****President [[Rodrigo Duterte]] rejects the prospect of reopening the country during a televised cabinet meeting. He goes on to claim that following the examples of the [[United States]]', [[Brazil]]'s and others' "bold actions" would result in "pandemonium", and the potential resultant spike in COVID-19 cases would land the nation in "deep shit". [https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/pky359/philippines-deep-shit-follows-trump-bolsonaro-reopening-duterte (Vice)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****Indonesia announced the biggest daily rise of 2,657 new [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases, taking the nationwide tally to 70,736. [[West Java]] reported the highest surge with 962 cases. This significant increase comes from the [[Officer Candidate School (Indonesian Army)|Army’s Officer Candidate School]] (Secapa) cluster. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/-indonesia-sees-highest-single-day-spike-covid-19-cases/1904936 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia]]
****Interim [[President of Bolivia|Bolivian President]] [[Jeanine Áñez]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-bolivia-anez/bolivias-president-anez-has-tested-positive-for-coronavirus-idUSKBN24A3EZ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]] 
****[[Diosdado Cabello]] confirms he tested positive for COVID-19. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/venezuela-socialist-party-boss-announces-covid-19-71702747 (ABC News)]

;International relations
*[[India–Nepal relations]]
**[[Nepal]] decides to block broadcasts of Indian news channels in Nepal with the exception of [[Doordarshan]] News, effective immediately. The move comes in the wake of reports on Nepal carried by some Indian news channels, including their allegedly "defamatory shows" on [[Nepali Prime Minister]] [[KP Sharma Oli]] along with the Chinese envoy. [https://thehimalayantimes.com/nepal/indian-news-channels-face-a-broadcasting-ban-in-nepal/ (''Himalayan Times'')]
*[[Chinese intelligence activity abroad]]
**In its annual report, [[Germany]]'s domestic intelligence agency [[Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution|BfV]] warns consumers that personal data they provide to Chinese payment companies or other tech firms, such as [[Tencent]], [[Alibaba Group|Alibaba]] and others, could end up in the hands of [[government of China|China's government]]. [https://wrex.com/2020/07/09/german-intel-warns-against-giving-data-to-chinese-tech-firms/#:~:text=BERLIN%20(AP)%20%E2%80%94%20Germany's%20domestic,the%20hands%20of%20China's%20government.&text=The%20head%20of%20the%20BfV,can%20only%20warn%20against%20this.%E2%80%9D (WREX)]

;Law and crime
*[[Supreme Court of the United States]]
**The court rules in ''[[McGirt v. Oklahoma]]''  and ''[[Sharp v. Murphy]]'' that nearly half of [[Oklahoma]] is [[Indian reservation|Native American tribal land]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/09/us/supreme-court-oklahoma-mcgirt-creek-nation.html (''The New York Times'')]
**The court rules in ''[[Trump v. Vance]]'' that prosecutors in [[Attorney General of New York|New York]] can seek [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s financial records in a major case on the scope and limits of presidential power, but also ruled in ''[[Trump v. Mazars USA, LLP]]'' that lower courts had not properly assessed the [[separation of powers]] between [[United States Congress|Congress]] and the President when the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] attempted to similarly subpoena his tax returns. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/09/us/trump-taxes-supreme-court.html (''The New York Times'')]
*Governor of [[Khabarovsk Krai]] [[Sergey Furgal]] is arrested by [[Russian police]] over a series of murders of several businessmen in 2004 and 2005 in his region, according to the [[Investigative Committee of Russia]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/russian-governor-sergei-furgal-arrested-over-links-to-several-murders-12025221 (Sky News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Park Won-soon]], the [[Mayor of Seoul]], is found dead after being declared missing earlier the same day. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20200710000500325 (Yonhap News Agency)]
*[[Ministry of Finance (Ireland)|Irish Minister of Finance]] [[Paschal Donohoe]] is elected president of the [[Eurogroup]], beating the candidatures of Spanish Minister [[Nadia Calviño]] and of Luxembourgish Minister [[Pierre Gramegna]]. He will succeed [[Mário Centeno]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/irelands-paschal-donohoe-wins-eurogroup-presidency/ (''Politico'')]
